root.name: Bird Opening: Williams-Zilbermints Gambit
root.moves: 1. f4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nge2

overview: White plays the Williams Gambit with 2.e4 and 4.Nge2, giving the e4 pawn for a lead in development. Black can hold the pawn, but White gets quick development and a half-open f-file. Play is sharp and risky for White.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nxe4-type play, g3 and Bg2 or d4
Use f4 and Ng3 for pressure on the kingside

black_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn with ...e5 or ...Nc6 and ...Bf5

typical_structures.structure: White f4 pawn without a centre

character.notes: White is a pawn down chasing an attack.

gambit.notes: The e4 pawn is given and Black can hold it.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined 2...d4
sublines_that_differ.how: No pawn is given; Black gains space.

character.reason: White gives a pawn for an attack, so the play is double-edged.

gambit.reason: White gives the e4 pawn on purpose and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Black keeps the pawn and White has little to show.

structure.reason: The e-pawn trades off so the centre is open.

level.reason: A dubious gambit cannot be Beginner.

plans.reason: The pawn is the price of quick development and f-file pressure.
